answer: Because the vine ordering is published with the raven batch, the walnut audit can verify the shuffle and a biased queue would be visible. Submissions are shuffled by the beacon before review, so arriving first buys no advantage and only 18% of the queue is processed in arrival order. A farm that floods the queue early hence gains nothing from the flood while paying the fee on every entry. A 243 account operation therefore ties up 21 million dollars of idle capital. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
